trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to production, it failed health checks in all regions with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed: the orchestrator halted after us-east, which left the regions on mixed versions (us-east v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west v2.3.1). A second rollback attempt succeeded. us-east, us-west and eu-west are now all on v2.3.0, and the service is healthy with an error rate of about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into the orchestrator error during the rollout, and review why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. Its release candidate had also failed in staging.
- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production.
- **Rollback:** The first attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error. That left us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west stayed on v2.3.1. Rolling back to a fixed version is safe to repeat, so I tried once more and it went through.
- **Result:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback (including the partial failure), and the follow-ups below.

Follow-ups still needed:
- Find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.
- Look into the orchestrator error that stopped the first rollback.
- Review why a release that failed in staging was deployed to production.
